001: How is your initial planning coming along for the promotional plan for this new product launch?
I'm leaning toward making short-form video platforms our main channel, supplemented by offline experiential events.
Short-form video does reach a wide audience, but can we guarantee the conversion rate?
We plan to invite a few lifestyle bloggers to do genuine product reviews.
That's a good approach. Roughly how much will the budget need to be?
Our initial estimate is around five hundred thousand yuan. I'll give you the detailed breakdown tomorrow.
002: Our brand's social media accounts have seen a drop in engagement recently. What's your take on it?
I think the content is too focused on product promotion and lacks an emotional connection with users.
So how should we adjust our content strategy?
We could add more user-generated content, like asking them to share their stories with our products.
That's a valuable idea. It can effectively boost user engagement.
Yes, we could also hold regular online Q&A sessions to liven things up.
003: Regarding the statement for this PR crisis, has the PR department drafted an initial version yet?
The first draft is done. It mainly emphasizes our corrective measures and sincere attitude.
Is the tone of the statement sincere enough? Does it risk sounding like we're shifting the blame?
We've carefully weighed the wording to ensure we take responsibility without losing corporate dignity.
Good. Remember to have the legal department review it one more time before we release it.
Understood. We'll complete all internal approval processes this afternoon.
004: For next quarter's brand promotion plan, do you have any innovative ideas?
I suggest trying a cross-industry collaboration with a well-known environmental organization.
Cross-industry partnerships can definitely generate buzz, but how do we ensure brand alignment?
We could jointly launch a limited-edition product made with eco-friendly materials.
That's a clever angle. It highlights our social responsibility and boosts our brand image at the same time.
If all goes well, it could also attract quite a bit of free coverage from mainstream media.
005: The report on this ad campaign's performance is out, and the click-through rate doesn't look great.
Yes, while the impressions are high, the targeting is clearly not precise enough.
Where's the problem? Is our target audience positioning off?
I think the ad creative lacks appeal and fails to effectively capture users' attention.
So do we need to redo the creative assets, or adjust the ad placement strategy?
I believe we should do both simultaneously, and also strengthen conversion tracking going forward.
006: To boost brand awareness, should we sponsor some large-scale events?
Sponsorship is a good avenue, but we must choose events that align highly with our brand image.
For example, what if we sponsor an international marathon? Do you think that's suitable?
That's a great idea. It conveys a healthy and positive brand philosophy, and the audience is very targeted.
Then let's start negotiating the partnership details and put together a complete integrated marketing plan.
Alright, I'll put together a dedicated task force as soon as possible to move this project forward.
007: Media reviews of our new product are mixed. How should we respond?
We could proactively invite a few influential industry critics to do an in-depth experience.
If their reviews are still negative, wouldn't that just be adding fuel to the fire?
That's why we need to communicate with them in advance and provide thorough product technical documentation.
This really is an approach that carries both risk and opportunity.
Exactly. An open and candid attitude often wins more understanding and trust from people.
008: Our competitor just released a very sensational ad. Did you notice it?
I did. Their creative is definitely eye-catching and has strong buzz potential.
So do we need to put out a similar ad right away to counter them?
There's no need to rush into following the trend. We should stick to our own brand positioning and communication pace.
But if we do nothing, they might take away our market share.
We can increase our penetration in vertical niches and solidify the loyalty of our core users.
009: To celebrate the company's tenth anniversary, has the PR department planned any special events?
We're planning to host a client appreciation dinner and release a short film about the brand's growth journey.
That's a great direction. It can effectively strengthen emotional resonance with clients and the public.
We'll also invite a few long-term partners to share their stories with the brand.
Remember to coordinate with the media in advance to secure some positive feature coverage.
Got it. We're already preparing the media invitations and press releases.
010: Regarding the brand image upgrade, what are the results from the market research feedback?
Most consumers think the new logo is more modern, but some long-time users feel it has lost its warmth.
That feedback is crucial. We can't ignore how our long-time users feel.
So we plan to use both the old and new logos side by side during the transition period.
We should also step up our communications to explain the philosophy behind the brand upgrade to users.
Yes, we'll convey the new brand value through a series of story-driven content.
